original_value: The article is devoted to the substantiation of approaches to the effective use of advantages and minimization of disadvantages and losses of e‑learning as a mean of forming mathematical competence of students in the conditions of research-oriented educational process. As a result of the ascertaining experiment, e-learning has certain disadvantages besides its obvious advantages (adaptability, possibility of individualization, absence of geographical barriers, ensuring social equality, unlimited number of listeners, etc.). However, the nature of these drawbacks lies not as much in the plane of opportunity itself as in the ability to use them effectively. On the example of the e-learning course (ELC) “Mathematical Analysis” (Calculus) of Borys Grinchenko Kyiv University, which is developed on the basis of the Moodle platform, didactic and methodical approaches to content preparation and organization of activities in the ELC in mathematics are offered. Given the specifics of mathematics as a discipline, the possibility of using ELCs to support the traditional learning process with full-time learning is revealed, introducing a partially mixed (combined) model. It is emphasized that effective formation of mathematical competence of students by means of e-learning is possible only in the conditions of research-oriented educational environment with active and concerned participation of students and partnership interaction. The prospect of further research in the analysis of e-learning opportunities for the formation of students’ mathematical competence, in particular, research and investigation tools, and the development of recommendations for the advanced training programs of teachers of mathematical disciplines of universities are outlined.

result.paraphrase: The article substantiates approaches to the effective use of e-learning advantages and to reducing its drawbacks and losses as a means of forming students’ mathematical competence in a research-oriented educational process. The ascertaining experiment showed that, alongside obvious benefits such as adaptability, individualization, no geographical barriers, social equality, and an unlimited number of learners, e-learning also has certain shortcomings. However, these drawbacks stem less from the possibilities themselves than from the ability to use them effectively. Using the e-learning course (ELC) “Mathematical Analysis” (Calculus) at Borys Grinchenko Kyiv University, developed on the Moodle platform, the article proposes didactic and methodological approaches to preparing content and organizing activities in mathematics ELCs. Considering the specifics of mathematics as a discipline, it shows that ELCs can support traditional face-to-face learning by introducing a partially blended model. It is emphasized that effective formation of students’ mathematical competence through e-learning is possible only in a research-oriented educational environment with active, interested student participation and partnership-based interaction. The article also outlines prospects for further research into e-learning opportunities for developing students’ mathematical competence, particularly research and investigative tools, and for developing recommendations for advanced training programs for university teachers of mathematical disciplines.
